answer:
I completed the analysis. Here are the results:

## Incident Counts and Rates by Zone

I counted the incidents in each zone (point-in-polygon) and computed the rate per 1,000 residents:

| Zone | Population | Incidents | Rate per 1,000 |
|------|-----------|-----------|----------------|
| **Z2** | 830 | 19 | **22.89** |
| Z5 | 7,400 | 66 | 8.92 |
| Z1 | 5,200 | 41 | 7.88 |
| Z4 | 2,600 | 18 | 6.92 |
| Z6 | 3,900 | 25 | 6.41 |
| Z8 | 6,100 | 37 | 6.07 |
| Z7 | 1,500 | 9 | 6.00 |
| Z3 | 4,100 | 22 | 5.37 |
| Z9 | 2,800 | 14 | 5.00 |

**The zone with the highest rate is Z2, at 22.89 incidents per 1,000 residents.**

This is driven by its very small population relative to its incident count.

**Notes on the data:**
- 256 total incidents were processed; 251 fell within the 9 zones and 5 fell outside any zone (unmatched).
- The incident counts per zone are also mapped as a choropleth on your interactive map, and the rate layer is available as a downloadable GeoJSON.

**Artifacts produced:**
- Incident counts per zone: [incidents_per_zone.geojson](https://agent/files/file_ac105722bdb1/download) and [table CSV](https://agent/files/file_4668b715c442/download)
- Zone rates table: [zone_rates.csv](https://agent/files/file_120f427875e6/download)
- Rate choropleth layer on the map: [incident_rate_per_1_000_residents.geojson](https://agent/files/file_f338d0f8a33b/download)
